read_ranges.scope: entire note including all theorem proofs, applications, conclusion and references

topic_relevance.A01: direct: the work studies sums of ratios in binary fractional programs and exact submodularity conditions for each single-ratio term.

definitions.name: single-ratio set function
definitions.statement: h(S;a,b)=(Σ_{i∈S}a_i)/(b_0+Σ_{i∈S}b_i) on a downward-closed feasible family F.

definitions.name: submodularity on F
definitions.statement: Diminishing returns; equivalently the two-element discrete second difference is nonpositive when S∪{i,j}∈F.

definitions.name: standing structural assumptions
definitions.statement: A1 denominators are strictly positive on F; A2 a_i≥0,b_0≥0,b_i>0; A3 F is downward closed.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 1 (necessary and sufficient submodularity criterion)
assumptions: A1 denominator positive for every feasible set
theorem_cards.statement: h is submodular on F iff for every admissible S and distinct i,j not in S with S∪{i,j}∈F, h(S∪{i})+h(S∪{j})≤a_i/b_i+a_j/b_j.
proof_steps: Substitute the diminishing-returns condition into the ratio formula.
Cross-multiply only positive denominators, then rearrange to obtain the stated pairwise threshold condition.
Reverse the algebra to get the equivalence.
gaps: The theorem is for one ratio with a positive intercept b_0; the paper separately shows homogeneous ratios with b_0=0 need not be submodular.

theorem_cards.label: Proposition 1 (monotonicity suffices)
theorem_cards.statement: If h is monotone nondecreasing over F, then h is submodular over F.
proof_steps: Monotonicity is rearranged to h(S)≤a_j/b_j for every admissible added item j.
Apply this to i and j and use Theorem 1’s criterion.
gaps: Sufficiency only; the paper provides a counterexample showing submodularity does not generally imply global monotonicity.

theorem_cards.label: Proposition 3 (homogeneous-ratio obstruction)
assumptions: Some feasible S contains at least three items with distinct a_i/b_i
theorem_cards.statement: Under these assumptions h is not submodular.
proof_steps: Compare the weighted averages after adding the largest-ratio item.
The resulting inequality contradicts diminishing returns.
gaps: This is a sufficient obstruction, not a full characterization when b_0=0.

theorem_cards.label: Proposition 4 (assortment sufficient condition)
assumptions: MMNL finite-support setup described in Section 4.1
Positive choice weights and revenue data as in the model
theorem_cards.statement: If revenue spread (r_max−r_min)/r_min is bounded by the minimum no-purchase odds over feasible assortments, the revenue function is nondecreasing and submodular.
proof_steps: Rewrite the spread condition as r_max q(S;v)≤r_min.
Bound current assortment revenue above by r_max q(S;v).
This gives the marginal monotonicity condition; Proposition 1 yields submodularity.
gaps: Application-specific sufficient condition; the paper’s industry discussion uses contextual assumptions rather than a universal empirical claim.

constant_dependence.explicit: Theorem 1 has no approximation constant. Greedy guarantees cited for monotone submodular maximization include 1−1/e under cardinality constraints; Proposition 6 has its own ratio-spread condition.
constant_dependence.dependence: Submodularity test depends on pairwise ratios a_i/b_i and current feasible-set numerator/denominator A_S,B_S; no estimate for the central maximal operator follows without a separate model mapping.

endpoint_limits.positive_intercept: Theorem 1 requires b_0>0. The authors’ Proposition 3 establishes non-submodularity for a common b_0=0 case with three distinct item ratios.
endpoint_limits.denominator: Strict positivity is needed everywhere on F for ratios and cross multiplication.
endpoint_limits.feasible_family: The stated diminishing-returns equivalence and applications use downward-closed F.
endpoint_limits.objective: The multiple-ratio objective is a sum of these single-ratio terms; the submodularity certificate is checked term by term.

reusable_methods.method: Test a ratio set function using discrete second differences and positive-denominator cross multiplication
reusable_methods.transfer: Relevant only when a finite discretization genuinely has 0–1 choices and a linear-over-linear score with b_0>0. It does not certify a continuous cube supremum or the maximal-cube operator.

reusable_methods.method: Turn monotonicity into a tractable sufficient test for submodularity
reusable_methods.transfer: For a finite search layer, bound every current ratio by each admissible item marginal ratio; preserve the exact feasible family.

unchecked: I read the full paper and manually checked the algebraic equivalence in Theorem 1 under positive denominators, along with the monotonicity implication. I did not independently derive the cited 1−1/e greedy guarantee or validate the paper’s external application data; those remain author-reported or cited results.
